inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page ordinary shares outstanding at 2026-11-05 (FY2026 10-K: 286,695,097) plus the 2M dilutive impact of share-based arrangements from the FY2026 EPS note = 288.7M fully diluted. This replaces the prior build's 293M (Q3 FY26 diluted weighted average), which lagged the buyback. FY2026 diluted weighted average was 294M. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge it. Buybacks (FY26 $1,892M, 9M shares) far exceed SBC ($168M) -- the excess is capital return funded out of the modelled FCF, value-neutral here. The count is ~6 weeks later than the balance sheet; implied post-year-end repurchases are small (<$0.1B) and not adjusted in net debt.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement, share-based compensation expense $168M (FY2025 $149M, FY2024 $127M); 0.84% of revenue. Cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement are not disclosed separately and TE publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line; immaterial (<0.1% of revenue) and not added.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 actual $1,892M (10-K cash-flow statement and repurchase table, 9M shares); FY2025 $1,347M. $2.5B of authorisation remained at fiscal year end. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.fy0_basis: FY2026 actual, fiscal year ended 2026-09-25 (10-K): net sales $19,885M (+15.2% reported, +11.9% organic, FX +2.2%, acquisitions +1.6%), after an $87M one-off reduction for IEEPA tariff refunds to be passed back to customers (offset by a $91M cost-of-sales credit; net $4M). reported_fcf $3,403M = operating cash flow $4,525M less capital expenditures $1,122M. The prior build's FY2026E estimates (revenue $19,823M, FCF $3,300M, SBC $172M) are replaced by these actuals.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> CoE 9.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5%, 18% tax -> 3.7% after tax; market-value weights ~92% equity / 8% debt -> 9.3%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: auto cyclicality, China concentration and AI customer concentration are charged in the bear flows and the 20% bear weight, not in a rate premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost already sits inside operating expense (and therefore EBITDA); operating lease liabilities ($491M at FY25) are EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment (B-equivalent), no double-charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests immaterial; flows are consolidated = attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). Unchanged from the 2026-10-02 build; TE is a design-in connector/sensor manufacturer, not a financial, REIT or holdco. UPDATE of 2026-11-19: FY0 moved from FY2026E (9 months + guided Q4) to FY2026 ACTUAL (10-K, year ended 2026-09-25). Changed: (1) anchors -- base revenue, net debt, diluted shares, SBC, owner FCF, buybacks; (2) year-1 (FY2027) growth in all three scenarios, on the 10-K outlook of double-digit sales growth with organic growth 'consistent with fiscal 2026 levels' (11.9%), a Q1 FY27 sales guide ~14.6% above the prior-year quarter and backlog up 36% to $8,388M; (3) year-1 capex, on the 10-K guide of ~6% of sales; (4) two equity-bridge deductions the 10-K now quantifies (pension deficit, acquisition earn-out). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth for years 2-10, every EBITDA-margin path, D&A, capex for years 2-10, cash-tax path, working-capital capture, WACC, terminal growth and cap multiples, and the 20/50/30 weights -- see inputs.unchanged_assumptions. BASE YEAR is the reported year rather than a mid-cycle revenue base: the revenue level is largely structural (Richards in the base; AI data-center revenue with Digital Data Networks at $3.2B, +44%) and Transportation (half of sales, +4.5% organic) is not at a volume peak. What IS near-peak is the MARGIN (GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC = 26.1% of sales in FY26 vs ~20-24% in 2017-2024), so the mid-cycle judgment is applied there: the base fades margin to 25.5% and the bear to ~23.5%. Interest income ($90M FY26) NOT stripped: TE is net-debt ($3.9B), so the strip rule does not apply and the flows are unlevered EBITDA-based anyway. EBITDA definition: GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC, i.e. restructuring ($117M FY26, recurring at TE every year) and acquisition costs ($32M) are left IN as operating costs. Pending Astrodyne TDI acquisition (~$1.4B cash, ~$250M sales, close expected by end CY2026, excluded from the Q1 guide): its revenue is inside FY27 growth, so its purchase price is deducted in equity_bridge.

unchanged_assumptions.growth_years_2_to_10: Left as built. FY27 guidance says nothing about FY28+; base still glides 7% -> 3%. Would move on: a multi-year AI/data-center revenue target beyond the current one, or two more quarters of book-to-bill at or below 1.0.
unchanged_assumptions.ebitda_margin_paths: Left as built. FY26 actual pre-SBC EBITDA margin was 26.1% against the 26.0% estimated in October, so the anchor did not move. Would move on: FY27 margin holding above ~27% through a quarter of flat Industrial growth (raise the through-cycle level), or Transportation segment margin staying near Q3 FY26's 17% (lower it).
unchanged_assumptions.cash_tax_path: Left at 18% -> 20%. FY26 GAAP effective rate 17.6%; cash taxes paid $454M are only ~11% of operating income, so the path is conservative on a cash basis. Would move on: disclosure that the cash/book gap is structural rather than timing.
unchanged_assumptions.wc_capture_pct: Left at -17%. FY26 actual trade working-capital build was ~$265-300M on $2,623M of added sales (-10% to -12%), helped by a $595M payables increase; the stock ratio is 21.9% of sales (AR 3,839 + inventory 2,962 - AP 2,455). One favourable year is not enough to lift it. Would move on: a second year below -12%.
unchanged_assumptions.da_and_capex_years_2_to_10: Left as built. FY26 D&A 5.2% and capex 5.6% of sales match the October estimates.
unchanged_assumptions.wacc_terminal_and_weights: Left at 9.3% / 2.0-3.0% / 13-17x and bear 20 / base 50 / bull 30. The risk-free input was not re-struck; no evidence in the 10-K bears on them.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.0-5.5%) diverges >30% from EPS (10-22%) and owner-FCF (11-12%) CAGRs. Equity is depressed by $1-2B/yr of buybacks plus dividends, so book value is not the compounding measure here. The EPS 3yr figure starts from a restructuring-heavy FY2023 ($6.03). Revenue 5yr CAGR (FY21-FY26, includes Richards and ~2pp of FX in FY26) remains the selected anchor; the through-cycle organic rate in TE's business model is ~4-6%.
historical_growth.notes: FY windows end FY2026 (audited, 10-K). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - SBC; SBC is 0.6-0.9% of revenue so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.1pp -- SBC is not funding the growth.

base.wc_capture_note: Trade NWC (AR $3,839M + inventory $2,962M - AP $2,455M at 2026-09-25) is 21.9% of sales. FY26 actual build was -10% to -12% of incremental revenue, flattered by a $595M payables increase; -17% retained. Growth consumes cash.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY26 actual pre-SBC EBITDA 26.1% (GAAP operating income $3,991M + D&A $1,033M + SBC $168M on $19,885M). Held ~26% while the AI order book converts, then faded to 25.5% as a through-cycle level: assumes one ordinary auto/industrial down-year inside the horizon rather than perpetual peak margin. Path unchanged from October.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A 5.2% of sales in FY26 includes acquired-intangible amortisation (Richards); capex 5.6% in FY26, guided to ~6% of sales for FY27 (10-K liquidity section) -- year 1 set to 6.0%, then the unchanged glide to 5.0% (FY17-25 range 4.3-6.7%).
base.growth_rationale: Year 1 raised 9% -> 13%: organic ~12% per the 10-K outlook, plus ~1pp Astrodyne part-year, plus ~0.4pp from lapping the $87M tariff-refund reduction, less a small haircut for a full-year view given with one quarter guided. Years 2-10 unchanged.

bull.growth_rationale: Year 1 raised 12% -> 15% (Q1 FY27 guide is already ~14.6% above the prior-year quarter before Astrodyne). Years 2-10 unchanged.

bear.growth_rationale: Year 1 raised 2% -> 6%: the first half is largely covered by the guided Q1 and an $8.4B backlog, so the AI-capex pause and China auto break now land in the second half of FY27 and in FY28 (-4%, unchanged). Year-1 capex 5.8% (guided 6% trimmed as the downturn arrives).

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 revenue +13%: organic growth near FY26's 11.9% as the company guides, plus a part year of Astrodyne TDI. The backlog ($8.4B, up 36%, two-thirds of it Industrial) and a Q1 guide of ~$5.35B carry the year; Digital Data Networks (AI cloud, $3.2B, +44%) and Energy (+18% organic) lead while Transportation grows a few points on content against flat global vehicle builds. Growth then glides from 7% to 3% as AI capex normalises and TE settles at its 4-6% organic business model plus bolt-ons. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin holds ~26% for two years and fades to a through-cycle 25.5%, i.e. FY26's record margin is not capitalised in perpetuity. Capex runs at the guided 6% of sales in FY27 before normalising. TE stays the solid number two to Amphenol in AI interconnect -- shares the growth, does not win it outright.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-center connectivity keeps compounding past the current build-out (power distribution and copper-in-rack hold up against optical), Industrial mix shift and the Richards/Astrodyne power adjacencies lift margin toward Amphenol-like levels (27.5% pre-SBC EBITDA; Industrial segment margin already rose from 17.7% to 20.4% in FY26), and auto content outperformance continues via high-voltage EV/hybrid platforms and Chinese OEM export programs. Revenue +15%/+10%/+9% then decelerates to 3.5%; terminal growth 3% and a 17x cap reflect a higher-quality, more secular mix.
scenario_narratives.bear: Two of TE's axes break at once, from the second half of FY27: a hyperscaler AI capex pause (or faster optical displacement of copper) stalls the fastest-growing piece of Industrial just as the record backlog proves cancellable, and a China auto price war plus tariff escalation hits the Asia-Pacific sales (39% of FY26 revenue) and the China share of auto. FY27 +6% (the guided first half plus Astrodyne, then a stall), FY28 -4%, with decremental margins taking pre-SBC EBITDA to 22.5% before recovering to a mid-cycle 23.5% (the 2017-2024 average band). Capex is cut to 4.8%. No solvency question -- net debt/EBITDA stays under 1x -- this is a cyclical earnings reset and a de-rating to a 13x cap, not a broken franchise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged at 20/50/30. Bear 20% (above the 15% default): two concentrated exposures -- a handful of hyperscale AI customers and China auto -- can turn simultaneously and the margin is at a record, so the down-cycle is more than a tail. Base 50%: FY27 guidance and the $8.4B backlog make the near-term path well-evidenced. Bull 30% (below 35%): the bull case needs AI to keep compounding AND margin to close the gap to Amphenol AND auto content to keep outrunning a weak production backdrop -- several independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF on the FY2026 actual base year, with the cyclical normalisation applied to MARGIN rather than to revenue. FY26 revenue is mostly structural (acquired Richards sales, a design-in AI book backed by a record backlog) and Transportation is not at a volume peak, so rebasing revenue to a mid-cycle level would discard real, contracted growth. The record ~26% pre-SBC EBITDA margin, by contrast, is a peak-ish number for a business that ran 20-24% in 2017-2024, so the base fades it to 25.5% and the bear resets it to 23.5% after a FY28 downturn. Risk is charged once: a single 9.3% USD WACC across scenarios, with cyclicality and customer/China concentration expressed in the bear flows and a 20% bear weight. Terminal values use a 13-17x cap appropriate to a high-quality cyclical industrial; Gordon at 9.3%/2.5% is ~15x, so the base cap and Gordon nearly coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI data-center demand concentrated in a few hyperscalers; a capex pause or optical-over-copper shift would hit the fastest-growing, highest-margin revenue
China and wider Asia-Pacific (39% of FY26 sales), exposed to the domestic auto price war and US-China tariffs
Margin is at a record; the base still assumes ~25.5% pre-SBC EBITDA through the cycle versus 20-24% historically
Share loss to Amphenol in AI interconnect, where it has out-executed on growth, margin and M&A
Bolt-on M&A cadence (Richards $2.3B, Astrodyne $1.4B) raises integration and capital-allocation risk; acquired growth is only value-creating if bought below the 9.3% WACC
FY27 growth rests on one guided quarter and a qualitative full-year outlook; backlog is not a firm commitment and can be rescheduled or cancelled
